categories.description: Errors where the model incorrectly identifies or assigns core attributes such as shape, color, or numerical values to objects or events.

sub_categories.description: Incorrectly labeling or recognizing 3D shapes, substituting correct shapes with incorrect ones (e.g., icosahedron for tetrahedron).
Assigning incorrect or non-existent colors to shapes or objects, or misordering color transitions.
Assigning incorrect numerical values to positions, shapes, or events, including fabricating numbers not present in the ground truth.
Inventing attributes (e.g., colors, shapes, events) not present in the ground truth, leading to invalid reasoning paths.
Incorrectly associating a shape, its color, and its timestamp, leading to mismatched or invalid event sequences.

categories.description: Errors involving incorrect mapping of events to time, misordering of sequences, or misunderstanding of temporal structure.

sub_categories.description: Incorrectly assigning start/end times or durations to events, leading to inaccurate sequencing or duration calculations.
Incorrectly ordering events, shapes, or numbers in time, resulting in mismatched associations or invalid conclusions.
Misidentifying when sequences begin/end relative to pauses, leading to inclusion or exclusion of incorrect data.
Misunderstanding the order or nature of events (e.g., assuming simultaneous appearance when events are sequential).
Assuming uniform or arbitrary time intervals without evidence, contradicting provided variable timing data.

categories.description: Errors arising from misreading, misrecording, or fabricating input data such as numbers, words, or timestamps.

sub_categories.description: Misreading or fabricating numerical values, shapes, or timestamps from the video or scene description.
Misrepresenting shuffled words or sequences (e.g., wrong letters, spacing, length) leading to invalid tracking.
Using incorrect or inconsistent indexing (0-based vs 1-based) leading to misaligned position calculations.
Inventing numbers, sequences, or events not present in the ground truth to force a plausible narrative.
Ignoring or overlooking part of the provided data, resulting in truncated or inaccurate analysis.

categories.description: Errors stemming from misunderstanding the problem’s scope, intent, or structure, leading to irrelevant or incorrect reasoning.

sub_categories.description: Misinterpreting what the question asks (e.g., tracking visibility vs. drawing duration).
Misunderstanding key terms (e.g., 'between' meaning positional sequence vs. numerical range).
Treating irrelevant visual aids (e.g., color palettes) as part of the solution or misinterpreting their purpose.
Assuming a static or limited view of the scene, failing to account for full sequences or total items.
Failing to recognize discrete units (e.g., 5-number sequences) or temporal boundaries (e.g., pauses).

categories.description: Errors that originate from earlier mistakes and cascade through subsequent reasoning, leading to invalid final conclusions.

sub_categories.description: Carrying forward incorrect assumptions, states, or inputs into later calculations, compounding inaccuracies.
Performing correct logic or arithmetic on incorrect data, yielding numerically plausible but factually wrong results.
Final sequence or answer is entirely incorrect due to accumulation of multiple prior misidentifications.
Attempting to salvage flawed reasoning with alternative interpretations (e.g., absolute difference) without correcting root causes.

sub_categories.sub_category_name: Final Answer Based on False Premise
sub_categories.description: Concluding with a wrong answer derived from a chain of incorrect assumptions or observations.

categories.description: Errors resulting from incomplete observation, miscounting, or failure to track all relevant elements in the scene.

sub_categories.description: Failing to accurately count items due to omission, misidentification, or including phantom elements.
Ignoring or failing to account for the full set of data (e.g., all 20 dominoes or all shuffles).
Not recognizing that an object persists and changes over time, instead treating transitions as new objects.
Treating a dynamic, time-based process as a single static frame, missing temporal details.
Disregarding clearly provided numerical, temporal, or visual data, pretending it is unavailable.
